HACKGPT / 01

Start here

Install the signed APK, find the main controls, and send a first message.

Toolbar

  1. Model Settings opens the provider setup and saved model controls.
  2. Model Selection opens the searchable picker.
  3. Chat History opens saved conversations and bulk actions.
  4. Appearance opens theme, font size, and send mode.
  5. Balance shows the active provider’s amount when available. Tap the Routr badge to switch between compact and exact credits.
  6. New Chat starts a conversation. Hold the plus for about five seconds for creator credits.

First message

  1. On Android 8.0 or newer, open the signed APK and confirm installation. Allow installs from your browser or file manager if asked.
  2. Open Select model and choose Demo → Beam 1.0 Free.
  3. Type a message. Tap the pulsing marker above the field if the circle is hidden, then tap the circle to send.

Install the signed update over your existing app to keep your chats. The pulsing up-arrow in the toolbar appears when a newer release is available. Tap it, download the APK, and open it to update.

GitHub releases

Message composer

  1. The label shows the active model, then its provider.
  2. Type or paste your draft in the message box.
  3. Tap the pulsing line to reveal the control circle in regular send mode. Hold and drag the line sideways to move the circle.
  4. Drag the left elbow up or down to resize the input.
  5. The right elbow resizes the same input. Use whichever side is easier to reach.
HACKGPT / 02

Connect a provider

The plug loads models. The disk saves your provider and model choices.

Connect with an API key

  1. Open the Settings gear, then tap + (6) to add a provider.
  2. Choose the provider type (3), then give it a name (2). For Kenari, choose Custom (OpenAI-compatible).
  3. Confirm the base URL (4). For Kenari, enter https://kenari.id/v1.
  4. Paste the API key you already have (5), then tap the plug (7) to load the catalog.
  5. Check the models to include, then tap the disk (8) to save. Open Model Selection to use them.

See the loaded model controls.

  1. Saved providers. Tap a card to edit it. Its number shows how many models are saved.
  2. Provider name. Enter the display name you want in the model picker.
  3. Provider type. Choose OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, or Custom for another OpenAI-compatible service.
  4. API base URL. Presets fill it in. For Custom, use the service’s HTTPS base URL.
  5. API key. Paste your provider key. Leave this field blank when editing to reuse an existing saved key.
  6. New provider (+). Open a blank provider configuration.
  7. Connect (plug). Check the connection and load models. Filter the list and check the models you want in chat.
  8. Save (disk). Save the configuration and checked models after connecting.

In the newer test APK the grid shows up to three complete rows. Swipe inside it for more. Swipe a card left to remove it after confirmation. The play button tests checked models and may incur charges.

HACKGPT / 03

Manage the loaded models

These controls appear inside Provider Settings after you connect and load a catalog.

What each control does

  1. Filter models. Search the loaded catalog by model name or ID.
  2. Provider Settings. Open this popup from the first gear. Select a saved provider or connect a new one to see its catalog.
  3. Test selected models. Tap play to send a test request to each checked model. Provider charges may apply.
  4. Select all or none. Toggle the entire loaded catalog. Filtering changes which rows you see. Check individual rows if you want only a subset.
  5. Retrieved models. Scroll this list. Check the models you want in the chat picker, then save.
  6. Disconnect. Disconnects this provider and removes its saved API key. Reconnect with a key to use it again.
  7. Model and test counts. Selected / total shows how many models are checked. Green counts passed tests and red counts failed tests. Both can be zero before testing.
HACKGPT / 04

Pick, inspect, and retest

The picker groups checked models by provider.

Read the model picker

  1. Select Model popup. Open it using the list icon. Search by model name or ID, then tap an available model.
  2. Provider counts. The line above Search shows how many models each provider contributes to the picker.
  3. Failed test. A red strikethrough and timestamp mark the last failed response test. Tap the row to inspect it and retest.
  4. Kenari group. These models use the saved Kenari connection. Rows tagged Image generation produce images.
  5. Routr group. These models use the saved Routr connection. The highlighted row is the active model.

Inspect a model

  1. Selected Model Details. Hold a model row to open the card. It can show context capacity, input types, image generation support, and pricing when supplied by the provider.
  2. Test Response. Tap play to test this one model. The request can use credits. A successful retest clears a failure mark.

Practice selecting, inspecting, and retesting

Search for a model, then tap to select it or hold its row to see details above the list. Use Play to test it. Try glm-5.3-flash for a successful response or glm-5.3 to practice a failure and retest. These outcomes are simulated.

Choose a model to begin.

Send and swipe

The floating circle sends messages and has four directional shortcuts.

Regular mode

Tap the pulsing marker to reveal the circle. Tap the circle to send. Enter adds a line.

Enter-to-Send

Enable it in Appearance. Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line when supported. Tap the chat twice and hold the third touch to reveal the action circle.

Practice a swipe

Drag the dot or tap an arrow. Each direction lights up the matching shortcut below.

Open the Android file picker.

Save the open conversation as Markdown.

Select the text in the draft.

Open the draft-clear confirmation.

Hold the marker and drag sideways to move the circle. Release near the middle to snap it to center. Drag either top corner of the composer vertically to resize it. The circle fades after about two idle seconds. Use the square above the field to stop a regular reply.

HACKGPT / 06

History and appearance

The clock opens saved chats. The half-filled circle opens Appearance.

Chat History

Manage and export chats

  1. Chat History popup. Open it with the clock in the main toolbar. Hold a row to show bulk controls, then tap more rows to add or remove them.
  2. Search chats. Filter by title, message, or attachment name.
  3. Select All. Toggle all results currently shown by the search.
  4. Bulk export. On Android, save a ZIP with one Markdown file per selected chat. To export one open chat, swipe down from the composer circle.
  5. Bulk delete. Review the confirmation before deleting the selected chats.
  6. History list. Scroll through your conversations. Tap a row to reopen the chat when selection mode is off.
  7. Single entry. Outside selection mode, swipe right to open the rename dialog or left to open the delete confirmation.

Appearance

Appearance controls

  1. Open Appearance from the half-filled circle in the toolbar.
  2. Choose Dark for a dark background.
  3. Choose Light for a light background.
  4. The return arrow toggles Enter-to-Send.
  5. Move the slider left for smaller chat text or right for larger text. The value on the right shows the current size.

On Android, the corner icon toggles Full screen.

Markdown filenames start with the chat’s UTC timestamp. Exports preserve formatting, diagram source, attachment names, and available response details.

HACKGPT / 07

Carry context across models

When you switch models during a chat, choose how much of the earlier conversation the next model receives.

Summarize a conversation

  1. After you receive a reply, stay in the same chat. Open Model Selection from the toolbar and choose a different model. The handoff card appears below the latest reply, with both model names shown (1).
  2. Choose how much context to share. Full history passes earlier messages and replies. A summary passes the condensed text, so details it leaves out may need to be restated. Fresh start sends your next prompt without earlier context. Your old messages remain visible.
  3. At a summary level, pick the previous model (2) or the incoming model (3) to write the summary.
  4. Tap Play (4), then review the summary before sending your next message. Triple-tap the summary field to edit it.

Generated images. If the next model supports image input and an eligible image is available, check Include latest generated image to send it as a separate reference with your next message. Summary levels only condense the text. Leave the box unchecked to skip the image, or choose Fresh start to skip both the image and earlier text.

Try the context slider

Imagine you just asked what a confusion matrix is. Move the slider to see how much of the example reply the next model would receive. This demo shows prepared summaries immediately. In the app, use Play to generate one.

Full historyFresh start

  1. Full history

    The next model receives the complete earlier conversation.

    A confusion matrix compares the labels a classifier predicts with the actual labels. Imagine a spam filter that checks 100 emails. In this example, rows are actual labels and columns are predictions. Of the 30 spam emails, the filter flags 24 as spam and lets 6 through. Of the 70 legitimate emails, it incorrectly flags 4 and correctly lets 66 through. If spam is the positive class, the four counts are 24 true positives, 6 false negatives, 4 false positives, and 66 true negatives. A false positive sends a real message to the spam folder. A false negative lets spam through to the inbox. Accuracy is the share of all emails classified correctly, which here is (24 + 66) / 100 = 90%. Precision answers a different question: of the 28 emails flagged as spam, how many were actually spam? The answer is 24 / 28, or about 86%. Recall asks how much of the actual spam the filter caught. That is 24 / 30, or 80%. These measures help you decide how to tune the filter. A stricter definition of spam could protect more legitimate messages but let more spam through. A more aggressive filter could catch more spam but wrongly flag extra legitimate messages. The matrix shows which error you are trading for the other.
  2. Light summary

    Keeps the main explanation, example, and trade-off.

    A confusion matrix compares predicted and actual labels. For a filter checking 100 emails, 24 spam messages are correctly flagged (true positives), 6 slip through (false negatives), 4 legitimate messages are wrongly flagged (false positives), and 66 are correctly allowed (true negatives). Accuracy is 90%. Precision is about 86% because 24 of the 28 flagged messages were spam. Recall is 80% because the filter caught 24 of 30 spam messages. The matrix helps compare the consequences of missed spam and wrongly blocked legitimate mail when tuning the filter.
  3. Medium summary

    Keeps the core idea and key numbers.

    A confusion matrix counts correct predictions and errors by class. In the spam example, the filter catches 24 spam emails, misses 6, wrongly flags 4 legitimate emails, and correctly allows 66. Accuracy is 90%, precision about 86%, and recall 80%.
  4. Strong summary

    Keeps only the central idea.

    A confusion matrix compares predicted and actual labels to show what a classifier gets right and which errors it makes.
  5. Fresh start

    The next model receives your next prompt with no earlier chat context.

Context levels at a glance

  1. Full history. The next model receives the complete earlier conversation.
  2. Light summary. Keeps the main explanation, example, and trade-off.
  3. Medium summary. Keeps the core idea and key numbers.
  4. Strong summary. Keeps only the central idea.
  5. Fresh start. The next model receives your next prompt with no earlier chat context.
